subject: general
question: The upward and downward growth of a plant is due to which of the following tropisms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Geotropism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Geotropism** is the growth of plant organs in response to gravity.
 
• Roots exhibit **positive geotropism**, growing downward towards gravitational pull.
 
• Shoots exhibit **negative geotropism**, growing upward away from gravitational pull.
 
• This response helps plants to anchor in soil and obtain necessary nutrients and water.
 
• The hormone **auxin** plays a significant role in geotropic responses by redistributing growth in plant cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phototropism**

 
 
• It is the growth of plant organs in response to light.
 
• Shoots usually show positive phototropism by growing towards light sources.
 
 
 
• **Hydrotropism**
 
 
• It refers to the growth of plant roots towards moisture or water.
 
• This response helps plants maximize water uptake from the soil.
 
 
 
• **Chemotropism**
 
 
• It involves growth or movement in response to a chemical stimulus.
 
• An example is the growth of pollen tubes towards ovules during fertilization.
 
 
 
• **Plant Hormones**
 
 
• Plant hormones like auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, ethylene, and abscisic acid regulate various growth responses.
 
• Auxins are key in phototropic and geotropic responses, influencing cell elongation.
